transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-30
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (CTO - Nebula), Maya (ML Eng), Samir (SRE), Rina (PM)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping for latency/throughput SLOs. Focus on TTFT (time to first token) vs TPOT (time per token), define p95/p99 targets, agree on workload sizing (seq lengths, concurrency, batch sizes), and a measurement/benchmark plan for the 2-week POC. Action items and next steps captured.

Topics covered (high level):
- Definitions and why TTFT vs TPOT matter for Nebula's user experience
- Current production profile and constraints (sequence lengths, concurrent requests, token mix)
- Target SLOs at p95/p99 and acceptable tradeoffs vs cost
- Measurement plan: replay vs synthetic, harness, telemetry and dashboards
- POC timeline and success criteria

Transcript (selected excerpts, auto-transcribed, some noise/errors):
[00:00] Jordan: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, happy holidays if we, if anyone is out, um we'll keep this tight. intro quick - Jordan here, AE at Redwood, with Priya our SE.
[00:08] Alex: hey thanks Jordan, quick note, we got a new hire Rina on product who'll be watching this POC.
[00:12] Priya: hi all yeah so goal today is to scope latency and throughput SLOs for your POC, specifically you mentioned TTFT and TPOT in the form-fill. want to confirm definitions and measurement plan.
[00:22] Maya: yeah, TTFT is the first token latency, that's most visible in our chat client. TPOT, we call it token gen time, so basically per-token after first. we care about both because first token feels like snappiness, TPOT affects long responses.
[00:34] Samir: also want to understand variance/cold starts. some of our spikes are 15-20% cold because of autoscale.
[00:40] Priya: totally, so for POC we usually measure: TTFT p95 and p99, TPOT p95 and p99, throughput in tokens/sec and requests/sec at target concurrency, and also cache hit rates (prefix/K-V cache).
[00:51] Jordan: can I ask what you're aiming for? i think your form had <200ms p95 TTFT but can you confirm?
[00:56] Alex: right historically we've seen about 350ms avg TTFT on current infra, we'd like p95 under 250ms ideally, p99 under 600ms. but cost is a factor so we may accept p95 300ms if TPOT is good.
[01:10] Priya: okay that's helpful. for context with Redwood Hosted and Dedicated we typically see TTFT in the 80-300ms range depending on model and quantization; TPOT depends on model size and batching. smaller models and quantized runtimes give lower TPOT.
[01:24] Maya: our workload: median seq length 32 tokens, 95th seq 160 tokens, 99th around 600 tokens (these are user chats + system prompts), average response length ~ 120 tokens. concurrency currently ~120 concurrent users during peak which translates to ~450 rps across endpoints.
[01:45] Priya: that's good detail. for bench we'll need a workload file with prompt distribution and seq length histogram - can you provide a 48h replay sample?
[01:54] Maya: yes we can anonymize and upload.
[01:56] Samir: question on batching - our concern is that aggressive batching lowers cost but increases TTFT for low-latency requests, how does Redwood suggest tradeoffs?
[02:04] Priya: by policy. Redwood routing can prioritize low-latency lanes with small batch sizes for interactive routes, and batch-heavy lanes for background tasks. There are autoscaling and burst policies too. recommended starting config: interactive route batch <=4, max wait 10ms; background batch up to 32. that's tunable.
[02:22] Alex: when you say batch wait 10ms, that's queueing delay, correct? any chance that could push TTFT beyond our p95?
[02:27] Priya: yes it's queue time. for POC we'll measure observed TTFT (queue + initial compute + network) and attribute components. we can show breakdown in console (queue | kernel | encode/decode).
[02:38] Jordan: let's talk SLOs — propose we target TTFT p95 250ms, p99 600ms; TPOT p95 45ms/token, p99 120ms/token for typical model (we'll firm model in bench). Does that sound in line?
[02:51] Alex: p95 250ms seems reasonable. TPOT 45ms/token good for smaller models but we need to anchor to your model profile.
[02:58] Priya: yes we will surface model profile (e.g., variant, quantization). For example, a 7B quantized runtime may hit ~30-50ms/token while a 70B float/reg runtime is much higher. We'll run targeted runs.
[03:12] Rina: how will we validate under realistic spiky traffic? replay is ideal but we also want synthetic stress tests to probe tail.
[03:18] Priya: agree: plan is two parts - 1) replay 48h sampled production traffic to measure realistic SLO attainment; 2) synthetic stress tests that sweep concurrency and batch size to map tail behavior and find bottlenecks. both runs will collect TTFT/TPOT p50/p95/p99, requests/sec, tokens/sec, GPU util, cache hit rate, and cold-start fraction.
[03:36] Samir: do you provide test harness? we prefer an open-source harness or something we can run in our CI.
[03:41] Jordan: yes Jordan: we'll share our benchmark harness (k6 + small client wrapper + Redwood load runner examples) and a README. it's usually dockerized so you can run either in your project or we can run on our infra.
[03:52] Maya: we want the measurement windows to be at least 15 minutes per test point to get stable p99; is that okay?
[03:57] Priya: yes 15 minutes per point is our baseline; for very taily runs we may extend to 30 minutes. we'll also recommend warm-up periods and KV cache priming to measure steady-state vs cold.
[04:08] Alex: success criteria - we want production parity for critical endpoints: 1) TTFT p95 within 20% of current observed target (so <=250ms), 2) TPOT p95 under agreed threshold, and 3) average cost/token reduction >= 10% or at least cost-neutral.
[04:25] Jordan: i'll capture that: SLO attainment + cost delta + operational runbook. if we meet these, next step is Dedicated pilot.
[04:31] Rina: timeline?
[04:33] Priya: recommended POC timeline: Week 0 (this week) - scoping + infra prep; Week 1 - run replay and baseline runs; Week 2 - stress runs, tuning (batching/quantization) and final report. 2 week POC total.
[04:47] Samir: about security — we will need SOC2 docs, SAML/SSO info, and dedicated VPC peering for the dedicated run.
[04:55] Jordan: we'll share SOC2 attestation link and security package. for dedicated we support VPC peering + customer-managed KMS.
[05:03] Alex: any gotchas around measuring TTFT when using streaming? our client opens stream and shows tokens as they arrive.
[05:08] Priya: streaming changes measurement: TTFT measured until client receives first byte/token. we instrument client-side timestamp + server-side timestamp to correlate. we'll provide a small client shim to capture that.
[05:19] Maya: what about LRU/kv cache hit expectations? we rely on prefix caching for many repeated system prompts.
[05:23] Priya: we'll measure cache hit rate; if hit rate > 70% your effective TPOT and overall cost drop significantly. we'll include KV cache priming step in the harness.
[05:33] Jordan: any other risks?
[05:35] Alex: major risk is production traffic shape — long-tail sequences can blow up token compute. also quantization artifacts — we need quality checks.
[05:43] Priya: agreed — part of POC quality plan: run automated evals on a sample of prompts to detect regressions. if quantized model shows >1% quality regression vs baseline we'll flag.
[05:52] Rina: final ask, please include expected infra (GPU type, nodes) we need cost estimate.
[05:57] Jordan: will include a suggested infra matrix (A100 vs H100 vs L4), rough throughput numbers, and cost estimate for the POC run.
[06:04] Alex: okay great. recap and next steps?
[06:07] Jordan: recap: Jordan to send harness+readme+infra by Jan 4; Nebula to upload 48h anonymized traffic by Jan 6; schedule live benchmark week of Jan 10; goals: TTFT p95 250ms, p99 600ms; TPOT p95 45ms/token, p99 120ms/token (model-dependent), report with cost delta + runbook.
[06:27] Priya: any questions after this we'll follow up asynchronously in the shared doc. thanks everyone.
[06:31] Alex: thanks all, look forward to the runs.
